It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A decade of distilling success is being marked with special celebrations and a new limited-edition gin. Pocketful of Stones, an independent Cornish distillery and hospitality business, is celebrating its 10th anniversary this September with a month of events across its Cornwall venues, culminating in a birthday party at its Penzance bar. A limited-edition Caspyn Gin will be released to mark the occasion. Recommended reading New owners of Porthleven cafe deli ‘blown away’ by support for reopening Falmouth team unveil newest offering combining two restaurant concepts under one roof Bid to bring 'traditional Cornish food hub' to Helston (Image: Pocketful of Stones) Mike Cunliffe, co-founder of Pocketful of Stones, said: "Ten years on, it’s still slightly surreal to think that what began as four bartenders with a shared passion for good spirits has grown into the business it is today. "We’ve had plenty of memorable moments along the way, from choosing lobsters straight off the boats during a very Cornish ‘business meeting’, to Shaun disappearing down a dual carriageway on a branded delivery bike after our first trade show, but we’ve also built something we’re hugely proud of. "Launching our first whisky and creating the Hell’s Stone brand were real highlights, along with, of course, producing our own absinthe spoon. "It hasn’t always been easy, particularly through the mini-budget fallout, but Cornwall’s spirit, creativity and generosity have carried us through. "We’re incredibly grateful to everyone who has been part of the journey so far, and we’re looking forward to seeing what mischief the next decade brings." Pocketful of Stones is celebrating its 10th anniversary with a month of events and a limited-edition gin. (Image: Pocketful of Stones) Visitors and locals are invited to join the festivities, which will conclude with the official 10-year birthday party and the launch of Caspyn Ten on Sunday, September 27 at the Pocketful of Stones bar on Causewayhead in Penzance. Founded in 2016, the distillery has grown from a small-batch gin producer into an award-winning name in the South West’s food and drink scene. It now produces 23 handcrafted products across eight spirit categories, including Dr Squid Gin, Hell’s Stone Whisky, King of Prussia Spiced Rum and Morveren Absinthe. Each bottle is inspired by Cornish folklore and the surrounding landscape. Over the past decade, Pocketful of Stones has sold more than half a million bottles and hosted over 20,000 visitors for tastings at its three venues. It exports spirits to markets including Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Hungary. The business now employs 30 people and has invested more than £300,000 in new stills over the past 18 months, increasing production capacity more than fourfold and creating new jobs.
